title: Mega Staircase: The Unpinned Knight Finish
summary: Recognize the final mating pattern once the queen leaves the knight’s pin: the opponent’s own pieces close the king’s exits.

nodes.question: What changes after the queen leaves g1?
nodes.explanation: Begin after ...Qxh2 in the final seven-piece diagram. White has Kg6 and Ng5 against Kh8, Ng8, Be7, Qh2 and f5. The queen has left the g-file.

branches.title: Use the freed knight immediately
commentary: Begin after ...Qxh2 in the final seven-piece diagram. White has Kg6 and Ng5 against Kh8, Ng8, Be7, Qh2 and f5. The queen has left the g-file.
Nf7# is mate and the only move preserving a win in this exact diagram. The knight checks h8; Kg6 covers g7/h7; Black’s own knight occupies g8. Queen h2 cannot capture or block a knight check.

branches.title: Independent pawn capture misses mate
commentary: Begin after ...Qxh2 in the final seven-piece diagram. White has Kg6 and Ng5 against Kh8, Ng8, Be7, Qh2 and f5. The queen has left the g-file.
Kxf5 captures material but abandons the mating net around Kh8. The exact remaining position is winning for Black; the immediate Nf7 mate was the critical opportunity.

exercises.prompt: Why can the knight finally move from g5?
exercises.answer: The black queen has left g1 for h2. It no longer pins Ng5 against Kg6, so Nf7 can deliver a knight check that no interposition can stop.

startContext: Only the final seven-piece diagram after ...Qxh2 at 146s is verified in this short pattern lesson. The earlier eight/nine-piece queen staircase, promotion choices and queen sacrifice remain source context and still require larger-position analysis. This is a final-move comparison, not an exact proof of the full staircase.
